correctness: PASS on three shapes and seeds 42 and 43 for the independently written trusted kernel only

screening.interpretation: Screening suggests a slowdown; no speedup was confirmed, and timing noise remains unresolved.

compiler_review.ttir: Baseline has 24 loop trips with one dot per trip; trusted two-slab has 12 trips with two ordered dots per trip.
compiler_review.ttgir: The trusted loop carries 13 values versus 9 and uses more operand staging; this does not establish better overlap.
compiler_review.ptx: Matmul Inspector reports 397 versus 498 static instructions, 18 versus 36 cp.async copies, and 32 versus 64 mma.sync sites per compiled body.
compiler_review.sass: Matmul Inspector reports 432 versus 496 static instructions and 32 versus 64 HMMA sites per compiled body.
compiler_review.resources: Baseline versus trusted: 120 versus 129 registers per thread, zero spills in both, 24576 versus 49152 bytes shared memory.

dynamic_profile.method: One profiled FC1 launch per implementation with zero-valued FP16 inputs; separate from paired timing.

research_question: Can a different K-loop or operand-scheduling strategy reduce loop overhead without increasing registers or shared-memory allocation relative to the baseline?
measured_observations: Trusted correctness passed all six shape-seed cases; exact Muse source was not evaluated.
Dynamic SASS instructions fell by about 22.6%, branch instructions by 50%, and tensor-pipe instructions were unchanged.
Registers rose 120 to 129 per thread and shared memory rose 24576 to 49152 bytes; neither kernel spilled.
Median paired screening speedup was 0.94736x; all eight pairs favored baseline. A/A median absolute ratio deviation was 4.85%. No speedup was confirmed.
speculative_explanations: The higher register and shared-memory requirements could reduce occupancy or scheduling flexibility; occupancy and causality were not measured.
feedback_for_next_proposal: The trusted two-slab implementation reduced dynamic loop-related instructions yet screened slower while using more registers and twice the shared memory. Propose a substantially different compute mechanism that could retain lower loop overhead or improve operand scheduling without that resource increase. Explain the expected generated-instruction and resource changes, and label unmeasured occupancy explanations as hypotheses. This is not an evaluation of the exact Muse-generated source.
